general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **European Union/United States:** EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and US Trade Representative Katherine Tai signed the "Transatlantic Semiconductor Accord" in Brussels on November 26, 2026. The agreement establishes a unified tariff ceiling of 2% on specialized AI accelerators produced within G7 member states. The NASDAQ-listed semiconductor index rose 4.2% in pre-market trading on November 27. This creates a formalized economic barrier against non-G7 AI hardware, specifically targeting Chinese high-end chip exports. Financial Times

• **Philippines/China:** Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced on November 26, 2026, that the Philippine Coast Guard detained two Chinese survey vessels near the Second Thomas Shoal. The vessels were seized after violating a 12-nautical-mile exclusion zone established by Manila. Beijing's Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned the Philippine ambassador and issued a formal warning of "severe countermeasures." This escalation increases the risk of activating the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty, which would draw the US into a direct naval confrontation. Reuters

• **UN Climate Summit (COP31):** The UN Secretariat reported on November 26, 2026, that the "Global South Adaptation Fund" has reached $450 billion in committed capital. This total represents a 15% shortfall from the $520 billion target set by the G20 for the 2026-2030 cycle. A coalition of 22 African nations, led by Nigeria, announced they will delay ratification of the New Carbon Credit Protocol until the funding gap is closed. The funding deficit stalls global net-zero timelines by halting infrastructure transitions in emerging markets. BBC

Why it matters: Increased geopolitical fragmentation in trade and security is creating high-volatility environments for long-term capital allocation.
